title: Domestic safety screening documentation

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports asking permission to document and recording complaints, symptoms, signs, injuries and relevant history in the person’s words without interpretation.
user_facing_items.population: Women subjected to intimate partner violence or sexual violence; the handbook does not directly address people under 18 or men.
user_facing_items.setting: Health-care encounters including first-line support, history, examination and documentation.
user_facing_items.jurisdiction: International guidance requiring UAE legal, safeguarding and referral adaptation
restrictions: Exact for survivor-centred first-line support, consent to documentation, recording complaints, symptoms, signs and injuries, and history or examination only when clinically performed. It is not authority for universal screening or automatic reporting in the UAE.

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports listening, documenting needs and concerns, validating, assessing safety and recording support discussed without asserting abuse or imposing action.
user_facing_items.population: Women subjected to intimate partner violence or sexual violence; the handbook does not directly address people under 18 or men.

user_facing_items.jurisdiction: International guidance requiring UAE legal, safeguarding and referral adaptation
restrictions: Exact for survivor-centred first-line support, consent to documentation, recording complaints, symptoms, signs and injuries, and history or examination only when clinically performed. It is not authority for universal screening or automatic reporting in the UAE.
user_facing_items.rationale: Supports survivor-centred first-line support and needs context for domestic safety screening; no decision is generated.

user_facing_items.final_wording: Supports recording clinician suspicion, confidential disclosure opportunity and direct enquiry only when clinically indicated; it does not support universal screening.
user_facing_items.population: Adults presenting to emergency care where domestic abuse is disclosed or clinically suspected; the text focuses primarily on women.
user_facing_items.setting: Emergency department recognition, confidential disclosure, injury documentation and local safeguarding support.
user_facing_items.jurisdiction: United Kingdom emergency medicine; requires UAE legal and safeguarding adaptation
restrictions: Exact only for confidential, clinician-led enquiry where suspicion exists, documentation at disclosure, injury documentation and recording child-welfare concerns. It is not used for universal screening or automatic police, shelter or referral action.
user_facing_items.rationale: Supports recognition and clinician-entered concern context for domestic safety screening; no decision is generated.
